Write the agent rules, skills, docs and GitHub templates for a hackathon multi-agent framework. Work in /Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/cayenne. Be fast and concise; a teammate is waiting. Read the approved plan first: /Users/ellishewes/.claude/plans/setup-a-proper-agent-greedy-perlis.md (it is the source of truth for the workflow, commands, kick-off checklist and risks).

CREATE ONLY THESE FILES (others are editing other files in this directory right now; do not modify anything else, especially not `.claude/settings.json`, `.entire/*`, `hq*`, `tools/`, `.github/workflows/`; do not run git add/commit/push):
- `AGENTS.md` (canonical rules for every agent; Codex and Cursor read it natively; HARD LIMIT 90 lines, aim for ~70; short beats complete: research shows long instruction files make agents worse)
- `CLAUDE.md` (first line `@AGENTS.md`, then a short "Claude Code only" section)
- `README.md` (short: what the repo is, that it is a framework TEMPLATE prepared before the event (pre-event tooling; all product code is written during DurHack in a fresh repo created from this template), quickstart links)
- `.agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/hq-plan/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/hq-review/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/hq-ship/SKILL.md` (agentskills.io format: YAML frontmatter with `name` matching the directory and a one-line `description` saying when to use it; body = numbered steps with exact commands; each under ~60 lines)
- the symlink `.claude/skills` -> `../.agents/skills` (run `ln -s ../.agents/skills .claude/skills`; `.claude/` already exists)
- `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/PLAYBOOK.md`
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/task.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` (blank issues enabled), `.github/pull_request_template.md`

Style: plain English, short sentences, no fluff. Do NOT use em dashes or en dashes anywhere (use colons, commas, hyphens or new sentences). Commands in backticks. Don't write `<!-- entire-agent:begin -->` markers: `entire graph setup` will append its own managed block to AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md later.

The CLI (being built in parallel; document exactly this interface): `./hq board [--brief]`, `./hq claim N --agent <claude|codex|cursor>`, `./hq release N [--needs-human] [--note "..."]`, `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md [--draft]`, `./hq ship <PR> [--skip-review]`, `./hq check`, `./hq setup [--check]`, `./hq bootstrap` (once per repo). Windows: `hq.cmd` or `python tools/hq/hq.py ...`. Labels: status:{ready,in-progress,review,blocked,needs-human}, P0 (demo-critical) P1 P2, size:{S,M,L} (L = split it), type:{feat,bug,chore,spike,docs}, review:{pass,changes}, agent:{claude,codex,cursor}, lane:<name>, epic. Milestones: M0 Skeleton, M1 MVP demo path, M2 Prizes + polish, M3 Submission.

Issue body headings (the issue form labels MUST be exactly these so GitHub renders `### <label>` headings that hq parses): Goal, Acceptance criteria, Scope (files/dirs this issue may touch), Do not touch, Blocked by (`#12, #14` or `none`), Verify (commands or manual steps), Notes. In task.yml make Goal and Acceptance criteria required, default label `status:ready`.

AGENTS.md must cover, tersely:
1. Context lives in `docs/hack/BRIEF.md` (event, prizes, deadlines), `docs/SPEC.md` (what we build, demo path), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (stack, lanes, contracts), `docs/DECISIONS.md`. Read only what your issue needs.
2. The loop: one issue = one agent = one worktree/branch = one PR. Humans assign issues; never pick your own. Steps: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`; context before code (`entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"`, `entire brain brief "<task>"`, `entire why <file>:<line>` before rewriting code you did not write); build in small commits; `./hq check` must pass; `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`; `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature` then `entire trail ci-pr`; unless size:S run `entire review`, fix findings, `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass`, `entire trail ready`; humans say "ship it" then `./hq ship <PR>`. Full detail: `.agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md`.
3. Git rules: work only in your own worktree and branch; never commit on main (a hook blocks it); stage files by name (never `git add -A` or `.`); never revert, checkout, stash or delete changes you did not make; never amend or force-push pushed commits; rebase on `origin/main` before `./hq pr` and fix your own conflicts. Commit and push your own branch freely without asking.
4. Coordination: GitHub is the only shared state. Out-of-scope work becomes a new issue (`gh issue create`), not a drive-by edit. Progress notes go in issue comments. Stuck: `./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`. Contract changes (shared types, API shapes) need their own issue.
5. Definition of done: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open with evidence, review passed (unless size:S).
6. Issues are approved designs: do not run brainstorming, spec or plan-document rituals for issue work; plan inline and build.
7. Entire records every session and pushes transcripts with your commits: never paste secrets, tokens or .env contents into prompts or code. Do not disable Entire.
8. Commits: subject says what the product can now do (imperative, under ~60 chars), one logical change per commit; no AI attribution or co-author trailers (the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is added automatically and must stay); no em dashes.

CLAUDE.md "Claude Code only" section: in this repo the personal commit-message skill's draft, wait-for-approval and never-push steps do NOT apply (Ellis approved autonomous commits and pushes on your own branch on 2026-11-13); its style rules still apply. Superpowers: an issue is an approved design, skip brainstorming and do not write docs/superpowers specs or plans for issue work; use subagents sparingly (tokens). Skills are in `.claude/skills` (`/hq-work`, `/hq-plan`, `/hq-review`, `/hq-ship`).

Skills:
- hq-work: the full loop with exact commands, a PR body template (What changed / How verified with the `./hq check` tail / Risks / Screenshots), conflict handling (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`, re-run check), out-of-scope and stuck handling, the definition of done.
- hq-plan: turn BRIEF/SPEC/ARCHITECTURE into issues. Rules: 1 issue = 1 agent = 1 PR, size S or M (L must be split), parallel issues must have disjoint Scope paths, contracts and skeleton first in M0 (shared types, API stubs, CI check commands, deploy) with everything else `Blocked by` them, P0 = on the demo path. FIRST show the human a table (title, lane, P, size, milestone, scope, blocked by) and wait for approval, THEN create each with `gh issue create --title ... --body-file <file> --label status:ready|status:blocked --label P1 --label size:S --label type:feat --label lane:<x> --milestone "M0 Skeleton"`, body using the exact headings. Create blockers first so their numbers exist.
- hq-review: review someone else's PR in a separate worktree/workspace: `gh pr checkout <PR>`; read the linked issue's acceptance criteria; `gh pr diff`; `./hq check`; run `entire review` if the `claude` and `codex` CLIs are available (it runs Claude Code + Codex reviewers and a judge from the shared profile and posts to the trail), otherwise review manually against the criteria. Post the verdict with `gh pr review <PR> --comment --body-file <file>` (you cannot approve your own account's PR), then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass --remove-label review:changes` or the reverse. Prefer a reviewer from a different vendor than the author (agent:* label).
- hq-ship: only when a human says ship. `./hq ship <PR>` (gates: CI green, review:pass, not draft, no conflicts); if refused, report the failing gate, don't force. After merge: `entire brain remember "<notable decision or lesson>"` when worth keeping; tell the human which issues got unblocked.

docs/hack/BRIEF.md: sections Event (DurHack 2026, MLH, ~24h; dates TBD), Deadlines (TBD: kick-off, code freeze = judging minus 3h, submission), Theme (TBD), Judging criteria (TBD), Prize tracks: read `.context/attachments/iE9vhH/pasted_text_2026-11-13_22-32-30.txt` and list each MLH track with a one-line "what qualifies" (ElevenLabs, Gemini API, Entire, Solana, Tiger Data, Vultr, DEV Writing Challenge, MongoDB Atlas) and a Target column (Entire: yes, via the workflow itself, using Sessions, Graph, Brain, Trails; others TBD). Constraints: MLH rules (only work done during the event is judged; this framework is disclosed pre-event tooling). docs/SPEC.md: placeholders (Problem, Users, Demo script: the 2-minute path judges see, MVP scope, Non-goals, Stretch). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: placeholders (Stack, Repo layout, Lanes table: lane | dirs | owner, Contracts: shared types/API shapes and where they live, Env vars (.env, never committed; Conductor copies via .worktreeinclude), Deploy). docs/DECISIONS.md: format `## YYYY-MM-DD: <decision>` with Context/Decision/Consequences, and 4 seed entries dated 2026-11-13: GitHub Issues as the single task queue; Entire for sessions, memory and review (branch checkpoint backend because the judging tool reads refs/heads/entire/*); squash merges keep Entire-Checkpoint trailers (repo squash message = PR title + commit details); fresh submission repo created from this template at kick-off.

docs/PLAYBOOK.md (humans; scannable; ~150-200 lines): Roles (Ellis owns main and demo build: deploy, freeze, tag demo-v1; both own lanes and merge their own lane's PRs; humans dispatch, agents never self-assign). Kick-off checklist (copy the 5 steps from the plan, exact commands). Phases (H0-2 plan: BRIEF/SPEC/ARCHITECTURE then /hq-plan then the M0 skeleton merged and deployed by ~H2; fan-out with ~3 agents each, add one only while waiting; sync every 2-3h for 10 min: `./hq board`, `entire dispatch --local`, re-plan, cut scope; overnight: optionally one unattended agent loop on one self-contained ticket with turn/budget limits; freeze ~3h before judging and tag `demo-v1`; submission). Dispatching an agent per tool: Conductor (⌘⇧N create workspace from the GitHub issue, then "work on #N" or /hq-work N); Cursor (start each agent in worktree mode, never two agents in one folder; Cursor inside Conductor may not fire Entire hooks so prefer Cursor IDE worktree agents or the `agent` CLI); Codex CLI (`git worktree add ../wt-N -b <you>/N-slug origin/main`, `cd ../wt-N`, `./hq setup`, `codex -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true "work on #N"`: Codex needs network for gh, git push and entire trail; or set `[sandbox_workspace_write] network_access = true` in ~/.codex/config.toml); Claude Code CLI (`claude -w` or a git worktree, then /hq-work N). Review and merge policy (cross-vendor review via entire review; review:pass can come from local entire review, hosted Trail review agents on entire.com (optional, needs credits: MLH promo code), or the other human's agent running /hq-review). Rate limits and tokens (spread work across Claude, OpenAI and Cursor subscriptions; cheaper models for chores; avoid agent teams/swarms; `entire session tokens`). Entire prize checklist (Sessions captured for all three agents; `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/entire/*'` shows entire/checkpoints/v1; Graph: agents use `entire graph query`, show `entire graph stats`; optional A/B: same issue in two workspaces with and without `entire graph setup --strict` to measure token savings; Brain: `entire brain brief` and `entire brain remember`; Trails per PR with `entire review` verdicts; Dispatch summaries; before making the repo public review transcripts with `entire checkpoint list` / `entire checkpoint explain`). Submission checklist (repo public after transcript review, README with run instructions and the pre-event tooling disclosure, demo video, Devpost, DEV post for the DEV Writing Challenge). Teammate onboarding (accept invite; install gh + `gh auth login`, Entire (`brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire` or `curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash`), `entire login`; plugins `entire plugin install graph` and `entire plugin install brain`; clone; `entire enable` in the clone (git hooks are per clone); `./hq setup` until all ✓; git user.email must match the GitHub account or Entire shows Unknown author; Codex users approve hooks once via `/hooks` and keep their main checkout on an up-to-date main because Codex reads `.codex/hooks.json` from the main checkout; Windows: enable Developer Mode and `git config --global core.symlinks true` before cloning so `.claude/skills` works, use `hq.cmd`; Cursor may also load Claude hooks from `.claude/settings.json`: if `entire status` shows duplicate sessions, turn off third-party hooks in Cursor). Troubleshooting (Codex hooks not active: fast-forward root checkout; commit on main blocked: create a branch, `HQ_ALLOW_MAIN=1` only for emergencies by the main owner; `./hq ship` refused: read the gate; keychain/network errors from entire trail inside a sandbox: rerun unsandboxed).

When done, report: files created with line counts (AGENTS.md must be ≤ 90 lines), and anything you were unsure about. Under 200 words.

1	# Plan: vendor-neutral multi-agent framework on GitHub Issues + Entire (DurHack)
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Ellis and one teammate are entering DurHack 2026 (MLH, ~24h). Each will run several coding agents
6	at once, a mix of **Claude Code, Codex (GPT) and Cursor**, coordinated through **GitHub Issues**.
7	With 6 to 10 agents live, the failure modes are duplicate work, file collisions, a broken `main`
8	before the demo, and agents stalling on process. Ellis also wants the workflow itself to be a
9	**Best Use of Entire** prize entry (Sessions, Graph, Brain, Trails). This change builds a
10	stack-agnostic framework now; hack-specific context (idea, stack, prize targets) comes next and
11	slots into placeholders.
12	
13	Decisions already made by Ellis:
14	- Entire is part of the workflow from the start (not bolted on later).
15	- Agents have full autonomy on their own branches: commit, push, open PRs without waiting.
16	  Direct commits to `main` stay blocked. House style kept (no AI trailers, no em dashes).
17	- Ellis invites the teammate to the repo himself.
18	- **Fresh repo at kick-off.** `ehewes/durhack-proj` becomes the framework **template repo**. At
19	  kick-off, the submission repo is created from it (`gh repo create --template`): no pre-event
20	  history, and Entire's judging tool sees only event sessions (a `clean_start` timeline, scored 4.5 vs 3.0).
21	- Teammate's OS and agents are unknown, so everything must work on Mac (with or without Conductor)
22	  and Windows, with any of Claude Code, Codex or Cursor.
23	
24	Verified current state:
25	- `ehewes/durhack-proj`: private, **remote empty** (nothing pushed). Local `main` = empty initial
26	  commit; branch `ehewes/new-conversation` adds Ellis's `Enable Entire` commit (`.entire/*`,
27	  `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, all Entire hook config).
28	- Entire CLI 0.13.4, enabled for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor. Checkpoint backend is `refs`
29	  (default). No Entire plugins installed (Graph, Brain missing). Git hooks live in the shared
30	  `.git/hooks` (commit-msg, post-commit, post-rewrite, pre-push, prepare-commit-msg); no
31	  `core.hooksPath`; **no pre-commit hook**. `entire status`: "Codex hooks are not active in this
32	  worktree" because Codex reads `.codex/hooks.json` from the **root checkout**
33	  (`conductor/repos/durhack-proj`, on `main`).
34	- `gh` 2.86 authed as `ehewes` (repo, workflow scopes). Default labels only. No rulesets.
35	- Ellis has Claude Code 2.1.322, Codex 0.166 (`codex review --base`, hooks, skills), Conductor
36	  (Claude + Codex bundled), Cursor app. Global: superpowers plugin, personal `commit-message` skill.
37	
38	## What the research found (sources in the research notes; the ones that shaped this design)
39	
40	1. **Plan first, then fan out.** Winning 2-person teams wrote a PRD and a ticket list (one ticket =
41	   one agent = one PR) in the first ~2h (Anthropic Build Day winners, Jun 2026; CERC Mar 2026).
42	2. **Ownership by directory/subsystem, contracts first.** Merge shared types, API stubs and a
43	   known-good template before anyone branches (Anthropic hackathon winners; Claude Code docs).
44	3. **Humans dispatch; agents don't self-select.** Cursor's and Anthropic's self-claiming experiments
45	   produced lock hoarding, avoided hard tasks and frequent conflicts.
46	4. **Every agent gets its own worktree, every vendor.** Codex ran `git checkout -- <file>` on other
47	   agents' files despite AGENTS.md (codex#6022); shared dirs wiped work.
48	5. **One short instruction file.** AGENTS.md is canonical (Codex and Cursor read it natively);
49	   CLAUDE.md = `@AGENTS.md`. Long prompts made agents "slower and dumber" (RepoMirror).
50	6. **"Done" = a runnable check with short output.** Agents claim success with failing tests.
51	7. **Cross-vendor review.** Each model finds more serious bugs in the other vendor's code (Greptile).
52	8. **~3 agents per person;** add one only while waiting. Each agent rebases and fixes its own
53	   conflicts (a dedicated integrator became the bottleneck).
54	9. **Protect main, deploy early, freeze ~3h before judging, tag a known-good commit.**
55	10. **Anti-pattern: too much process.** A heavy-scaffolding entrant's demo never worked.
56	11. **Entire judging tool** (`entireio/entire-judge`) only fetches `refs/heads/entire/*`, so the repo
57	    must use the `branch` checkpoint backend or it scores as "no session history". It also rewards
58	    work after event start, prompt quality, multi-session work and visible `entire` usage.
59	12. **Entire + squash merges:** links survive only if the squash commit keeps the
60	    `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers (set GitHub's squash message to "PR title + commit details").
61	13. **Conductor repo settings are per person**; the docs say commit the logic as a script and make
62	    each person's Conductor setup a one-line call to it.
63	
64	## Approach
65	
66	**One sensible way: a thin layer we own on top of GitHub Issues, with Entire as the memory,
67	review and attribution layer.** Ruled out:
68	- CCPM: Claude-only, and it creates its own worktrees inside Conductor's.
69	- beads, Backlog.md, Task Master: a second tracker next to GitHub Issues (Task Master is also stale).
70	- spec-kit, BMAD: process-heavy, the anti-pattern above.
71	- Gas Town, Agent Teams: hours of setup, very high token burn, single vendor.
72	
73	Ideas borrowed:
74	- from beads: the ready queue and the claim step.
75	- from CCPM: "files touched" and "blocked by" on issues.
76	- from spec-kit: the spec → tasks → issues flow.
77	- from Backlog.md: a definition of done.
78	- from Entire: `entire review` for cross-vendor review.
79	
80	## The workflow
81	
82	**One issue = one agent session = one worktree/branch = one PR.** GitHub is the only shared
83	state; `.context/` and Conductor workspaces are per-agent scratch.
84	
85	Agent loop (identical for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; full text in `.agents/skills/hq-work`):
86	1. Human picks an issue from `./hq board` and opens an isolated workspace (Conductor ⌘⇧N from the
87	   issue, a Cursor worktree agent, or a Codex/Claude CLI in its own `git worktree`), says
88	   "work on #N" or `/hq-work N`.
89	2. `./hq claim N --agent <claude|codex|cursor>` claims it, safely across humans; prints the issue,
90	   what else is in flight, and overlapping files.
91	3. Context before code: `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"`,
92	   `entire brain brief "<task>"`; `entire why <file>:<line>` before rewriting code it didn't write.
93	4. Small commits, files staged by name. Out-of-scope work becomes a new issue, not a drive-by.
94	5. `./hq check` must pass; its tail goes in the PR.
95	6. `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md` pushes the branch, opens the PR (`Closes #N`) and sets
96	   `status:review`.
97	7. `entire trail create --title "<title> (#N)" --type feature`, then `entire trail ci-pr` (links the PR).
98	8. Unless `size:S`: `entire review` (shared profile: Claude Code + Codex reviewers, one judge).
99	   Fix the findings, add the `review:pass` label, then `entire trail ready`.
100	9. Human says "ship it": `./hq ship <PR>` (CI green + `review:pass`) squash-merges with the
101	   checkpoint trailers kept, and unblocks dependent issues.
102	
103	Stuck: `./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`.
104	
105	Humans:
106	- Ellis owns `main` and the demo build (deploy, freeze, tag `demo-v1`).
107	- Both own lanes and merge their own lane's PRs.
108	- Both dispatch issues; agents never pick their own.
109	
110	## What gets built
111	
112	| Path | Purpose |
113	|---|---|
114	| `hq` + `tools/hq/hq.py` | CLI, python3 stdlib (3.9+) + `gh`; shim `exec python3 tools/hq/hq.py "$@"` |
115	| `tools/hq/tests/test_hq.py` | unittest for the pure logic (TDD) |
116	| `hq.json` | `lanes` (lane → owner), `check` + `setup` command lists (empty until stack), `stale_minutes: 60` |
117	| `AGENTS.md` | ≤ ~90 lines: where context lives, the loop, git rules, coordination, DoD, Entire use, commit style, "an issue is an approved design: skip brainstorm/spec rituals" |
118	| `CLAUDE.md` | `@AGENTS.md` + Claude-only: `commit-message` skill's draft/wait/never-push steps don't apply here (style does); don't write superpowers spec/plan docs for issue work |
119	| `.agents/skills/hq-{work,plan,review,ship}/SKILL.md` | agentskills.io skills (Codex + Cursor read `.agents/skills`); `.claude/skills` → symlink `../.agents/skills` for Claude |
120	| `docs/hack/BRIEF.md` | event, deadlines, judging, prize tracks (pre-filled from the MLH list), targets (TBD) |
121	| `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md` | placeholders: spec, demo path, stack, lanes, contracts; append-only decision log |
122	| `docs/PLAYBOOK.md` | humans: roles, phases, dispatch per tool, cadence, rate limits, overnight loop, freeze, submission + Entire prize checklist, teammate onboarding, troubleshooting |
123	| `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/task.yml` (+ `config.yml`) | Goal, Acceptance criteria, Scope (files/dirs), Do not touch, Blocked by, Verify, Notes |
124	| `.github/pull_request_template.md` | for PRs opened in the UI (hq builds its own body) |
125	| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | on PR + push to `main`: hq unit tests, `./hq setup --ci`, `./hq check` |
126	| `.githooks/pre-commit` | blocks commits on `main` (`HQ_ALLOW_MAIN=1` overrides); Entire uses no pre-commit, so no clash |
127	| `.conductor/settings.toml` | `setup = "./hq setup"` (plus the same one-liner set in each person's Conductor) |
128	| `.worktreeinclude`, `.gitignore` | `.env*`, `.entire/settings.local.json`; ignore `.env*`, `.context/`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, caches |
129	| `.claude/settings.json` | **merge** a `permissions` block into Entire's hook file (allow `./hq`, `gh issue/pr`, git basics, read/trail/review `entire` cmds; deny force-push, `entire disable/clean`) |
130	
131	### `./hq` commands
132	- `setup [--check|--ci]`: per clone/workspace. Checks python, gh auth, repo access, git email,
133	  Entire enabled + `branch` backend, guard hook, `gc.auto=0` (Entire worktree bug), and that the
134	  root checkout has `.codex/hooks.json`. Without `--check` it installs the guard into the shared
135	  `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, chaining any existing hook, sets `gc.auto 0`, and runs `hq.json` setup
136	  commands. `--ci` only runs the setup commands. Prints a ✓/✗ checklist with a fix for each ✗.
137	- `bootstrap` (once, Ellis), idempotent:
138	  - Labels:
139	    - `status:{ready,in-progress,review,blocked,needs-human}`
140	    - `P0` (demo-critical), `P1`, `P2`
141	    - `size:{S,M,L}` (L means split it)
142	    - `type:{feat,bug,chore,spike,docs}`
143	    - `review:{pass,changes}`
144	    - `agent:{claude,codex,cursor}`
145	    - `epic`, plus `lane:*` from `hq.json`
146	  - Milestones: M0 Skeleton, M1 MVP demo path, M2 Prizes + polish, M3 Submission.
147	  - Repo merge settings: squash only, title = PR title, message = commit details,
148	    delete branch on merge.
149	  - A **ruleset** on the default branch (PR required, 0 approvals, no force-push, no deletion).
150	    If GitHub refuses it (private repo without Pro), it says so and the pre-commit guard remains
151	    the protection.
152	- `board [--brief]`: one screen.
153	  - Sections: in progress (who / agent id / age / branch / PR), review (CI, verdict, conflicts),
154	    needs-human, blocked (by #), ready queue (lane → P → size).
155	  - **Overlap radar:** files touched by more than one open PR.
156	  - Stale claims: no activity for more than `stale_minutes`.
157	- `claim N --agent A`:
158	  - Refuses if the issue is closed, blocked (open `Blocked by` refs) or claimed by another id.
159	  - Posts `<!-- hq:claim id=<login>/<agent>/<workspace> branch=… -->`, re-reads, and backs off if
160	    an earlier active claim exists. Two humans share no lock, so earliest claim wins.
161	  - Assigns `@me`, sets `status:in-progress` and `agent:A`.
162	  - If on `main`, creates `<login>/<N>-<slug>`.
163	  - Prints the issue, what's in flight and overlapping files.
164	  - The workspace id comes from `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME`, else the worktree dirname.
165	- `release N [--needs-human] [--note …]`: release marker + note; relabel ready or needs-human;
166	  unassign if no other claim by me.
167	- `pr N --body-file F [--draft]`:
168	  - Refuses on `main`, and if behind `origin/main` (rebase first).
169	  - Pushes, then creates or updates the PR as `<issue title> (#N)` with `Closes #N` and the agent id.
170	  - Moves the issue to `status:review` and copies its `lane`/`P`/`agent` labels to the PR.
171	- `ship PR [--skip-review]`:
172	  - Gates: open, not draft, not conflicting, checks green (or none), `review:pass`.
173	  - `gh pr merge --squash`, with no local branch delete (it breaks in worktrees).
174	  - Relabels issues whose `Blocked by` refs are now all closed to `ready`, with a comment.
175	- `check`: runs `hq.json` check commands; ✓/✗ + seconds each; on failure prints the last 30 lines;
176	  exits 0 with a notice when none are configured.
177	- Issue bodies use fixed `### Goal / ### Acceptance criteria / ### Scope / ### Do not touch /
178	  ### Blocked by / ### Verify / ### Notes` headings, which the issue form and `hq-plan` both emit
179	  and hq parses.

183	these**, in this order, committing between steps. The reviewer found that `brain setup` silently
184	refuses a repo with uncommitted changes.
185	```
186	entire configure --checkpoint-backend branch      # committed settings → fresh repo inherits it; judge reads refs/heads/entire/*
187	entire plugin install graph && entire graph setup --repo .    # managed block in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md → commit
188	entire review --configure --set-agents claude-code,codex --set-judge codex --set-output trail   # shared profile → commit
189	entire plugin install brain && entire brain setup (no backfill / no daemon flags, checked via --help)
190	```
191	Review route for every teammate setup, including Cursor-only (no local `claude`/`codex`). The
192	`review:pass` label can come from any of three places:
193	- local `entire review`;
194	- the hosted Trail review agents on entire.com (optional; uses credits from the MLH promo code);

200	- `hq.cmd` shim for Windows (`python "%~dp0tools\hq\hq.py" %*`).
201	- Hooks are POSIX `sh`, which Git for Windows runs.
202	- The `.claude/skills` symlink needs `core.symlinks=true` (Developer Mode) on Windows. The
203	  playbook covers it; Cursor and Codex read `.agents/skills` directly.
204	- Workspace id falls back to the worktree dirname when there's no Conductor.
205

208	   Conductor and set the setup one-liner. Invite the teammate.

210	   with the `branch` backend are already committed. Ellis links the repo on entire.com for Trails.
211	3. `./hq bootstrap` (labels, milestones, merge settings, ruleset), then `./hq setup` on each machine.
212	4. Approve the Codex hooks once (`/hooks`). Close **every pre-kick-off agent session** and start
213	   fresh ones, because old sessions would date the timeline before kick-off.
214	5. Fill BRIEF, SPEC and ARCHITECTURE, then `/hq-plan` → the M0 skeleton issue first.

217	
218	I'll commit in house style and push without stopping for per-commit approval; approving this plan
219	covers that.

222	   - (A) `hq.py` + tests (TDD), to the command spec above.
223	   - (B) AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, skills + symlink, docs/*, issue and PR templates.
224	   - (C) CI, `.githooks`, Conductor, `.gitignore`, `.worktreeinclude`, `.claude/settings.json` merge.
225	
226	   Then I review it, run the tests, and commit in 3 stages: hq CLI, agent rules + docs, repo config.
227	2. **Entire block.** I run the commands above in order, commit between steps, and check that

253	- `./hq pr` gives a PR with `Closes #N` and the labels. Two PRs touching one file show up in the

Run a multi-agent review against the current branch or a --target branch:
several reviewer agents review the change in parallel, then a single judge consolidates their
reports into the final verdict in a closing round. Reviews are saved as named
profiles in Entire settings and clone-local preferences. On first run, guided
setup writes a profile and asks before starting agents.

Flags:
  --configure    set up a review profile (shows available agents + profiles).
                 With --set-* flags it writes the profile non-interactively;
                 otherwise it opens the wizard (interactive) without starting agents.
  --set-agents   with --configure: comma-separated reviewer agents for the profile
  --set-judge    with --configure: the consolidating judge as agent[=model]
  --set-output   with --configure: where the verdict goes: local (default) or trail
  --local        with --configure: save to .entire/settings.local.json (just you)
                 instead of .entire/settings.json (shared). Interactive setup asks.
  --set-task     with --configure: the profile's canonical task text
  --set-model    with --configure: per-reviewer model as agent=model (repeatable)
  --set-slot     with --configure: a reviewer slot as agent[=model] (repeatable;
                 the same agent/model may repeat to run it multiple times)
  --set-config   with --configure: a reviewer's own agent config as
                 reviewer=<config.json|isolated|none> (repeatable). It replaces
                 the reviewed checkout's hooks, MCP servers and extensions; the
                 checkout's skills still load. Saved to clone-local preferences.
  --edit         re-open the advanced profile skill picker
  --findings     browse local findings; pass a handle to print one saved run
---WHY
Explain the commit, checkpoint, prompt, and session behind a file or line.

Target a specific line with <file>:12 or the --line flag.

Usage:
  entire why <file>[:line] [flags]

Examples:
  entire why src/auth.go:42
  entire why src/auth.go:42 --json

Flags:
---CREATE
Create a repository-scoped project trail, then link its branch. In the current repository, publish the local branch first; no separate commit or push is required. Uses the current feature branch, or derives a new branch from the title when on the base branch. Use --branch to choose a branch, or --no-branch for intent only. With --no-branch, the current or --repo repository becomes the Trail scope and requires repository write access; --project without --repo creates unscoped intent instead. Repository writers can create scoped trails and link branches. Unscoped creation requires project management. With a branch, --idempotency-key applies only to linking; if linking fails, retry with trail link rather than creating another trail. With --repo, no local branch is published: link existing remote work or use --branch-action create to create it on the server from --base. This command does not commit changes, and does not change the local checkout unless --checkout switches to the published branch afterwards; otherwise it prints the git switch command when the linked branch is not the current one. Branches are preserved if creation fails.

Usage:
  entire trail create [flags]

Flags:
      --assignee strings         Assignee logins; replaces the complete list (--assignee= clears it)
      --base string              Base branch the change merges into; with --branch-action create, the new branch also starts from it
      --body string              Trail description (--body= clears it on update)
      --branch string            Branch to use (defaults to the current feature branch; create derives one from the title on the base branch)
      --branch-action string     Branch action: link existing remote work, or create a new branch (default "link")
      --checkout[=true|false]    Switch to the published branch after creating the trail
  -h, --help[=true|false]        help for create
      --idempotency-key string   Retry key for linking a branch; with intent-only creation, requires project management
      --json[=true|false]        Output raw JSON instead of a table
      --no-branch[=true|false]   Create intent scoped to the current or --repo repository; --project alone creates unscoped intent
      --priority string          Priority (urgent, high, medium, low, none)
      --status string            Lifecycle status (open, closed)
      --title string             Trail title
      --type string              Type (bug, feature, task)

Global Flags:
      --context name     Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
      --project string   Project as gh/<owner> or et/<project>; required for list, otherwise defaults to the repository's namespace
      --repo string      Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; for list, only filters the required --project
---TOKENS

# AGENTS.md

Rules for every coding agent in this repo: Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. Short on purpose.

## Context
- `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`: event, prizes, deadlines.
- `docs/SPEC.md`: what we build, the demo path.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: stack, lanes, contracts.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`: decisions so far.

Read only what your issue needs.

## The loop
One issue = one agent = one worktree/branch = one PR. Humans assign issues. Never pick your own.

1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <claude|codex|cursor>`.
2. Context before code: `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"`,
   `entire brain brief "<task>"`. Run `entire why <file>:<line>` before rewriting code you did not write.
3. Build inside the issue's Scope, in small commits.
4. `./hq check` must pass.
5. Open the PR: `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`.
6. Trail: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`, then `entire trail ci-pr`.
7. Unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`, fix the findings,
   `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass`, then `entire trail ready`.
8. Stop and report. Only when a human says "ship it": `./hq ship <PR>`.

Full detail: `.agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md`. Also useful: `./hq board`, `./hq setup --check`.
Windows: use `hq.cmd` or `python tools/hq/hq.py` wherever this file says `./hq`.

## Git
- Work only in your own worktree and branch. Never commit on `main` (a hook blocks it).
- Stage files by name. Never `git add -A` or `git add .`.
- Never revert, checkout, stash or delete changes you did not make.
- Never amend or force-push commits that are already pushed.
- Before `./hq pr`, rebase on `origin/main` (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`) and fix
  your own conflicts. If your branch is already pushed, `git merge origin/main` instead.
- Commit and push your own branch freely. No need to ask.

## Coordination
- GitHub is the only shared state. `.context/` is your private scratch.
- Out-of-scope work becomes a new issue (`gh issue create`), not a drive-by edit.
- Never edit paths listed under "Do not touch" in your issue.
- Progress notes go in issue comments: `gh issue comment N --body "..."`.
- Stuck: `./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.
- Contract changes (shared types, API shapes) need their own issue.

## Definition of done
- Every acceptance criterion is met.
- `./hq check` passes, with its tail in the PR body.
- The PR is open with evidence: what you ran and what you saw.
- Review passed (`review:pass`), unless the issue is `size:S`.

## Issues are approved designs
Do not run brainstorming, spec or plan-document rituals for issue work. Plan inline, then build.

## Entire
Entire records every session and pushes transcripts with your commits.
- Never paste secrets, tokens or `.env` contents into prompts or code.
- Do not disable Entire or remove its hooks.

## Commits
- The subject says what the product can now do: imperative, under ~60 characters.
- One logical change per commit.
- No AI attribution or co-author trailers. The `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is added
  automatically and must stay.
- No em dashes.

# hq-review

Review in your own worktree or workspace, never in the author's. Prefer a reviewer from a
different vendor than the author (the PR's `agent:*` label).

1. Check out the PR: `gh pr checkout <PR>`.
2. Find the issue: `gh pr view <PR> --json title,labels,closingIssuesReferences`, then
   `gh issue view <N>`. Note the Acceptance criteria, Scope and Do not touch.
3. Read the diff: `gh pr diff <PR>`. Flag any file outside Scope or inside Do not touch.
4. Run `./hq check` and the issue's Verify steps.
5. If `command -v claude && command -v codex` succeeds, run `entire review`. It runs Claude Code
   and Codex reviewers plus a judge from the shared profile and posts to the trail. Otherwise
   review by hand against each acceptance criterion.
6. Write the verdict to `.context/review-<PR>.md`:
   - Verdict: pass or changes.
   - Each acceptance criterion: met or not met, with evidence.
   - Findings, blocking first: `file:line`, the problem, a suggested fix.
   - The tail of `./hq check`.
7. Post it: `gh pr review <PR> --comment --body-file .context/review-<PR>.md`.
   Use `--comment`: you cannot approve a PR opened from your own account.
8. Label it:
   - pass: `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass --remove-label review:changes`
   - changes: `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:changes --remove-label review:pass`
9. Do not push fixes to the author's branch and do not merge. Tell the human the verdict.

   - Tell the human which issues got unblocked (`./hq ship` prints them; see `./hq board --brief`).

# Decisions

Append-only log, newest at the bottom. Add an entry when a choice would surprise a newcomer or is
costly to undo. Agents also record it with `entire brain remember "<decision>"`.

Format:

```
## YYYY-MM-DD: <decision>
**Context:** why it came up.
**Decision:** what we chose.
**Consequences:** what follows, good and bad.
```

## 2026-11-13: GitHub Issues is the single task queue
**Context:** Up to ~10 agents across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor need one shared view of the
work. A second tracker (beads, Backlog.md, Task Master) would drift from GitHub.
**Decision:** Every task is a GitHub issue in the task form. `./hq` claims, labels and ships them.
Humans dispatch; agents never pick their own.
**Consequences:** GitHub is the only shared state; `.context/` and workspaces are scratch. Every
agent needs `gh` auth and network access.

## 2026-11-13: Entire for sessions, memory and review
**Context:** We want shared session history, codebase mapping, persistent memory and cross-vendor
review, and we target Best Use of Entire. Entire's judging tool only reads `refs/heads/entire/*`.
**Decision:** Use Entire Sessions, Graph, Brain and Trails, and `entire review` (Claude Code and
Codex reviewers, one judge). Use the `branch` checkpoint backend.
**Consequences:** Every session is recorded and pushed, so no secrets in prompts. Each clone runs
`entire enable`. `review:pass` needs local `entire review`, hosted Trail review or `/hq-review`.

## 2026-11-13: Squash merges keep Entire-Checkpoint trailers
**Context:** Entire links commits to sessions through `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. A squash
message without them breaks the link.
**Decision:** Squash merge only. Repo setting: squash title = PR title, message = commit details.
`./hq ship` merges this way.
**Consequences:** `main` gets one commit per PR and `entire why` still resolves to sessions. Never
edit the trailers out of a squash message.

## 2026-11-13: Fresh submission repo from this template at kick-off
**Context:** MLH only judges work done during the event, and Entire's judging tool scores a clean
start higher.
**Decision:** This repo is a template. At kick-off we run `gh repo create --template` and hack in
the new repo.
**Consequences:** The submission has no pre-event history. Pre-kick-off agent sessions are closed
and fresh ones started. The README discloses the framework as pre-event tooling.

# Playbook (humans)

How the two of us run DurHack with 6 to 10 agents. Agents follow `AGENTS.md`. This file is for us.

## Roles
- **Ellis** owns `main` and the demo build: deploys, the code freeze, the `demo-v1` tag.
- **Both** own lanes (see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`) and merge their own lane's PRs.
- **Humans dispatch.** Agents never pick or self-assign issues.

## Cheat sheet
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `./hq board [--brief]` | One screen: in progress, review, needs-human, blocked, ready queue, overlap radar, stale claims |
| `./hq claim N --agent <you>` | Agent claims issue N (`<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`) |
| `./hq release N [--needs-human] [--note "..."]` | Gives an issue back, optionally asking a human a question |
| `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md [--draft]` | Pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N`, moves the issue to `status:review` |
| `./hq ship <PR> [--skip-review]` | Squash-merges if CI is green, `review:pass` is set, not draft, no conflicts |
| `./hq check` | Runs the project checks from `hq.json` |
| `./hq setup [--check]` | Prepares (or only checks) this clone or workspace |
| `./hq bootstrap` | Once per repo: labels, milestones, merge settings, ruleset |

Windows: `hq.cmd ...` or `python tools/hq/hq.py ...`.

Labels:
- `status:{ready,in-progress,review,blocked,needs-human}`
- `P0` (demo-critical), `P1`, `P2`
- `size:{S,M,L}` (L = split it)
- `type:{feat,bug,chore,spike,docs}`
- `review:{pass,changes}`, `agent:{claude,codex,cursor}`, `lane:<name>`, `epic`

Milestones: M0 Skeleton, M1 MVP demo path, M2 Prizes + polish, M3 Submission.

## Kick-off checklist (~15 min at event start)
1. Create the submission repo from the template and invite the teammate:
   ```
   gh repo create ehewes/<name> --private --template ehewes/durhack-proj --clone
   gh api -X PUT repos/ehewes/<name>/collaborators/<teammate-login> -f permission=push
   ```
   Add the repo to Conductor and set its setup script to `./hq setup`.
2. In the new clone, each person runs `entire enable`. Git hooks are per clone; the settings with
   the `branch` checkpoint backend are already committed. Ellis links the repo on entire.com for
   Trails.
3. Ellis runs `./hq bootstrap` (labels, milestones, merge settings, ruleset). Then each machine
   runs `./hq setup`.
4. Codex users approve the hooks once (`/hooks`). Close **every** pre-kick-off agent session and
   start fresh ones: old sessions would date the timeline before kick-off.
5. Fill `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`, `docs/SPEC.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, then run `/hq-plan`.
   The M0 skeleton issue comes first.

## Phases
**H0 to H2: plan and skeleton**
- Fill BRIEF, SPEC (demo script first) and ARCHITECTURE (lanes, contracts) together.
- Run `/hq-plan`, approve the table, let it create the issues.
- Dispatch M0: shared types, API stubs, `hq.json` checks, deploy. Merged and deployed by ~H2.

**Fan-out**
- Each human runs ~3 agents on ready issues in their own lane, P0 first.
- Add one more agent only while the others are waiting (CI, review).
- Watch `./hq board`: the overlap radar and stale claims.

**Sync every 2 to 3 hours (10 min)**
- `./hq board`, then `entire dispatch --local` for a summary of what the agents did.
- Re-plan: new issues via `/hq-plan`, re-prioritise, cut scope (drop P2, move work to Stretch).
- Answer every `status:needs-human` issue.

**Overnight (optional)**
- One unattended agent loop on one self-contained ticket, off the demo path, with turn and
  budget limits (for example `claude -p "work on #N" --max-budget-usd 5`). Review it in the morning.

**Freeze (~3h before judging)**
- Ellis tags the known-good build and deploys it:
  `git fetch origin && git tag demo-v1 origin/main && git push origin demo-v1`.
- After the freeze only demo-path fixes merge, each rehearsed on the demo script. Tag `demo-v2`
  if one lands.

**Submission**
- Work through the submission checklist below. Rehearse the demo from the tag.

## Dispatching an agent
Pick a ready issue from `./hq board`. One agent per worktree, always.

**Conductor (Mac):** ⌘⇧N, create the workspace from the GitHub issue, then say "work on #N" or
`/hq-work N`. The workspace setup script runs `./hq setup`.

**Cursor:** start each agent in worktree mode. Never two agents in one folder. Cursor inside
Conductor may not fire Entire hooks, so prefer Cursor IDE worktree agents or the `agent` CLI.
Prompt: "work on #N".

**Codex CLI:**
```
git worktree add ../wt-N -b <login>/N-slug origin/main
cd ../wt-N
./hq setup
codex -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true "work on #N"
```
Codex needs network for `gh`, `git push` and `entire trail`. To make it permanent, set
`[sandbox_workspace_write] network_access = true` in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

**Claude Code CLI:** `claude -w` (or the git worktree steps above), then `/hq-work N`.

Outside Conductor, copy `.env` into the new worktree yourself.

## Review and merge
- Every PR except `size:S` needs `review:pass` before `./hq ship`. `ship` only checks the label,
  so set it only after a real review.
- Cross-vendor: prefer a reviewer from a different vendor than the author (the PR's `agent:*`
  label). `entire review` runs Claude Code and Codex reviewers plus a judge.
- `review:pass` can come from:
  - local `entire review` (needs the `claude` and `codex` CLIs);
  - hosted Trail review agents on entire.com (optional, needs credits: MLH promo code);
  - the other human's agent running `/hq-review <PR>`.
- Lane owners merge their own lane's PRs: tell the agent "ship it", or run `./hq ship <PR>`.
- Contracts, deploy config and anything after the freeze: Ellis merges.

## Rate limits and tokens
- Spread agents across the Claude, OpenAI and Cursor subscriptions. When one rate-limits,
  dispatch the next issue to another vendor.
- Use cheaper models for chores and docs (`/model` in Claude Code and Codex).
- Avoid agent teams and swarms. One issue per session; start a fresh session for the next one.
- `entire graph query` costs far fewer tokens than blind file search.
- Check spend: `entire session tokens <session-id>` (ids from `entire session list`).

## Entire prize checklist
- [ ] Sessions captured for all three agents (`entire session list`, `entire status`).
- [ ] `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/entire/*'` shows `entire/checkpoints/v1`.
- [ ] Graph: agents use `entire graph query`. Show `entire graph stats`.
- [ ] Optional A/B: the same issue in two workspaces, with and without
      `entire graph setup --strict`. Compare `entire session tokens` to measure the savings.
- [ ] Brain: `entire brain brief` before tasks, `entire brain remember` after notable merges.
- [ ] Trails: one per PR, with `entire review` verdicts.
- [ ] Dispatch summaries: `entire dispatch --local` at each sync. Keep them for Devpost and DEV.
- [ ] Before making the repo public, review transcripts with `entire checkpoint list` and
      `entire checkpoint explain <id>`.

## Submission checklist
- [ ] Transcripts reviewed (above). No secrets in code, commits or sessions.
- [ ] Repo public: `gh repo edit --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences`.
- [ ] README: what it does, how to run it, the pre-event tooling disclosure.
- [ ] Demo video following the 2-minute demo script in `docs/SPEC.md`.
- [ ] Devpost: repo link, video, prize tracks from `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`.
- [ ] DEV post for the DEV Writing Challenge.

## Teammate onboarding
1. Accept the repo invite.
2. Install `gh` and run `gh auth login`.
3. Install Entire: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire` or
   `curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash`. Then `entire login`.
4. Plugins: `entire plugin install graph` and `entire plugin install brain`.
5. Windows, before cloning: enable Developer Mode and run `git config --global core.symlinks true`
   so `.claude/skills` works. Use `hq.cmd` instead of `./hq`.
6. Clone: `gh repo clone ehewes/<name>`, then `cd <name>`.
7. Run `entire enable` in the clone (git hooks are per clone).
8. `git config user.email` must match your GitHub account, or Entire shows "Unknown author".
9. Run `./hq setup` until every line is ✓.
10. Codex: approve the hooks once via `/hooks`. Keep your main checkout on an up-to-date `main`
    (`git pull --ff-only`): Codex reads `.codex/hooks.json` from the main checkout.
11. Cursor: it may also load Claude hooks from `.claude/settings.json`. If `entire status` shows
    duplicate sessions, turn off third-party hooks in Cursor.

## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `entire status`: Codex hooks not active | Fast-forward the root checkout: `git -C <root checkout> pull --ff-only` (Conductor: `~/conductor/repos/<name>`) |
| Commit on `main` blocked | Create a branch: `git switch -c <login>/N-slug`. `HQ_ALLOW_MAIN=1` is for emergencies, by the main owner only |
| `./hq ship` refused | Read the gate it names (CI, review, draft, conflicts), fix it, retry. Never bypass |
| `./hq claim` refused | The issue is closed, blocked or claimed by someone else. Check `./hq board` |
| Keychain or network errors from `entire trail` in a sandbox | Rerun unsandboxed (Codex: the network flag above) |
| Entire shows "Unknown author" | Set `git config user.email` to your GitHub email |
| Duplicate sessions from Cursor | Turn off third-party hooks in Cursor |
| No skills in Claude Code on Windows | `.claude/skills` arrived as a plain file: set `core.symlinks true` and re-clone |
